text:
maria: Quick async — final pass on the ship checklist. Infra and runtime are ✅ but two open items: (1) pricing/billing hooks for GA customers (quota enforcement + invoice tagging), (2) oncall routing for model-fallback incidents. Can owners ack and note blockers by EOD? :eyes:

sam: Infra side is green. Dedicated capacity autoscale test passed at 10k rps this morning. I linked the perf logs: https://internal.redwood/perf/3041 — no blockers from runtime. :thumbsup:

taylor: Oncall routing needs a small play change. Right now fallback to smaller model doesn't trigger a separate alert; we want an alert when fallback happens + an SLO-violation metric. I can add an alert rule but need the metric name from runtime team. Pinged @sam for metric name.

leah: Support docs: we still need a canned KB for billing disputes (overages) and a sample ticket template. Also want an FAQ about latency variance during burst autoscale. I started a draft here: https://docs.internal/redwood/shiproom/ship-kb-draft — please add comments.

maria: Pricing question — are we comfortable with the GA free tier quotas? Legal flagged potential abuse vectors if quotas are too generous. We should confirm enforcement mechanism (hard quota vs throttling) and what gets logged for billing disputes.

sam: We enforce via rate-limit + quota deduction in the billing pipeline. For GA I'd prefer hard quota (reject) for free-tier, throttling for paid. Billing webhook sends usage events with tags: customer_id, route, model_variant, tokens. Example payload: { "customer_id": "cust_123", "route": "text.generate", "model": "gpt-redwood-v1", "tokens": 234 } Let me know if you need additional fields.

leah: That payload looks fine. For support playbook we need a short decision tree: overage -> confirm webhook -> apply credit? I'll flesh it out and drop into the KB.

taylor: Re: alert on fallback — we can create an alert on metric runtime.fallback.count > 0 with tag model_variant!=primary. But we need the runtime to emit fallback.count with labels. Sam, any objections?

sam: No objections. We will add fallback.count and label fallback_reason. ETA for metric rollout: tomorrow morning.

maria: Great. Two last product checks: docs for customers on expected SLA (p99 latency under normal load, fallbacks explained) and the pricing page language (clear note about burst pricing and quota enforcement). Who owns the final wording?

leah: I'll own the customer-facing SLA doc and the KB verbiage. Need a single sentence for the pricing page to avoid legal rewrite loops — something like: "Burst usage may incur additional charges; free-tier requests are rate-limited and may be rejected when limits are reached." Thoughts?

sam: LGTM, ops note: include link to latency dashboard and link to incident contact for enterprise accounts.

maria: Ok owners: sam (runtime metrics + billing webhook), taylor (alerts + oncall routing), leah (support KB + customer SLA doc). Please confirm by 18:00 PT. If any of these are not done we mark the GA checklist as "docs/billing incomplete" and gate the launch.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: release/ga-canary -> prod at 2026-03-21T22:00:00Z. Status: scheduled.

maria: Noted. If any owner can't meet ETA call it out now so we can adjust the deploy window. :alarm_clock:

sam: Confirmed — metric rollout tomorrow 09:00 PT, webhook fields final by 12:00 PT.

taylor: Will have alert rules in place by 14:00 PT and update oncall routing before EOD.

leah: I'll push KB and the one-sentence pricing blurb by 16:00 PT.

maria: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll consolidate and post the final shiproom checklist after EOD. :white_check_mark:
